teachingReview.body: Nucleoside-naive adults generally receive 0.5 mg daily on an empty stomach. retainedBodies.heading: Address alcohol-associated malnutrition
retainedBodies.body: Alcohol cessation and adequate nutrition belong in the same plan. Review vitamin and trace-mineral needs, including thiamine, folate, pyridoxine, vitamins A and D, and zinc. Thiamine deficiency can cause Wernicke’s encephalopathy or Korsakoff syndrome; thiamine is used to prevent and treat these complications.

verifiedQuestions.question: Which error creates the greatest avoidable risk? Focus: tenofovir disoproxil.

verifiedQuestions.rationale: TDF can cause renal toxicity, including Fanconi syndrome, and loss of bone mineral density. Ignoring these risks can cause preventable harm. Kidney-based dosing, review of nephrotoxins, and monitoring after discontinuation address the book’s safety concerns.

retainedBodies.heading: Use entecavir correctly
retainedBodies.body: Nucleoside-naive adults generally receive 0.5 mg daily on an empty stomach. Food reduces its exposure, so the fasting instruction must be built into the daily schedule separately from dose selection.
